advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert validate()'s findings are in the canonical sorted (spelling, code, detail) order, not merely equal across identical-input runs.
evidence: tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py:238-239: `routes = [_route("show"), _route("show"), _route("x", capabilities=("nope",))]` then `assert [f.code for f in validate(routes)] == [f.code for f in validate(routes)]`
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py: `findings.sort(key=lambda f: (f.spelling, f.code, f.detail))` in validate() — the sort is the documented contract but the test would pass even if it were deleted
Docstring of validate() claims 'returning findings in a deterministic order' — the test compares identical inputs, not the actual canonical ordering
advisory.finding: test_findings_are_deterministic_in_order asserts validate(routes) equals validate(routes) on the same input, which is trivially true for any pure deterministic function and does not verify the documented sorted order. Removing the `findings.sort(key=lambda f: (f.spelling, f.code, f.detail))` line in validate() would still pass this test, so the 'deterministic order' contract is not actually protected.
scenarios: A future refactor removes or breaks the sort key ordering; the test still passes because same-input runs remain byte-identical regardless of sort.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct a route table whose findings are known to be emitted out of sorted order by the checks, then assert the returned list equals the explicitly sorted expected sequence of (spelling, code, detail) tuples.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider dropping the ignored `width` parameter from RebarHelpFormatter.__init__ (or document that it is intentionally overridden) so callers are not misled.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py:56: `width: int | None = None,` parameter is accepted
src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py:62: `width=_FIXED_WIDTH,` — the passed width is never forwarded
dropped.finding: RebarHelpFormatter.__init__ accepts a `width` parameter but silently discards it, always passing _FIXED_WIDTH to super().__init__. A caller passing width=N will be silently ignored, which can surprise future maintainers.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify or fix that RebarArgumentParser's non-termination guarantee does not cover the --help path (HelpAction still calls exit()/raises SystemExit).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py:75: `def error(self, message: str) -> None:` only overrides error(), not exit()
Docstring at src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py:71-72: 'here ``error()`` raises :class:`ParseError` so a library call never terminates the interpreter'
ABSENCE: no test exercises parse_args(['--help']); tests use format_help() instead (tests/unit/test_cli_parser_contract.py test_help_* use format_help())
dropped.finding: RebarArgumentParser only overrides error() to raise ParseError, but the docstring claims 'a library call never terminates the interpreter.' The -h/--help path (argparse HelpAction) calls self.exit() (not error()), which still raises SystemExit, so the non-termination guarantee is overstated for the help path.
dropped.suggested_fix: Either narrow the docstring to 'a parse failure never terminates the interpreter' or also override exit() to raise a catchable exception if the help path must be non-terminating.
